analysis.title: Event Pulse
analysis.question: Which ideas and engineering artifacts surface around AI conferences and hackathons—and which persist after the event echo fades?
analysis.summary: Event-linked programs, papers, projects, and selected public observations are analyzed as provenance contexts, with attention separated from technical substance and 30/90-day persistence checks.
analysis.executive_summary: 3 events currently have linked evidence. High event volume is not treated as corroboration: each dossier reports concrete artifacts, source concentration, and later independent follow-through separately.

events.name: AI Engineer World's Fair 2026
events.sampling_note: Bounded program sample capped at three sessions per configured priority track. It describes the selected engineering agenda, not the full conference program.
events.framing: Use the official program to measure which engineering problems occupied the agenda, then require artifacts or later independent evidence before treating repeated session language as technical corroboration.

attention.label: moderate
attention.interpretation: Observed event attention only; agenda size and social repetition do not establish quality or adoption.

technical_substance.label: limited
technical_substance.interpretation: Papers and repositories receive full artifact weight; hackathon submission pages receive partial weight until implementation is inspectable. Independent follow-through remains separate.

events.finding: The observed event record concentrates on Coding agents & developer tooling, Training, evaluation & self-improvement, Skills, protocols & integrations. It contains 0 artifact records across one source; this establishes what appeared around the event, not whether it became adopted.
events.why_it_matters: Use the official program to measure which engineering problems occupied the agenda, then require artifacts or later independent evidence before treating repeated session language as technical corroboration.
events.verification_read: Only event claims or observations are present; technical substance is not yet demonstrated.
events.next_confirmation: Look for independent repositories, deployment reports, benchmarks, hiring demand, or repeated cross-source evidence after the event.
events.counter_signal: The concept disappears after the event, remains confined to sponsor language, or produces no inspectable artifact or later independent use.

social_inbox.instruction: Add a public URL and an original observation to the reviewed social-link inbox; do not copy full post text.

method.purpose: Events are evidence contexts. They help explain where an observation appeared and whether it persisted after the room moved on; they do not become a parallel theme taxonomy or independent proof of adoption.
method.event_attention: Measures observed volume, source breadth, evidence-family breadth, and follow-through. It is an attention score, not a quality or adoption score.
method.technical_substance: Measures concrete artifacts, technical-record share, artifact diversity, and independent follow-through. A crowded agenda alone cannot earn a high score.
method.echo_control: Exact repeated titles or URLs inside one event are collapsed before breadth is counted. Several posts about one talk remain one underlying observation.
method.sampling: Every event discloses its collection boundary. Bounded samples describe only the selected record and are never presented as representative of the full event.
method.claims: Programs, talks, social posts, and sponsor descriptions establish what was presented or claimed. Papers, code, demos, and later independent evidence are shown separately.
method.persistence: Each completed event is revisited after 30 and 90 days. Absence of later evidence is reported as not observed, never silently treated as confirmation.
method.copyright: Store titles, short descriptions, public URLs, dates, authors, and analyst observations. Do not store full social posts, transcripts, or copied article bodies.
